microbenchmarks.note: perf05_size was added after the simulator run; it is measured on the board (5 samples) and in simulation once, outside the sampled sim run

applications.detail: First execution on any platform, 2026-09-22, in simulation through the production lifecycle with the workload-profile delta applied. b0compute and b0array completed with the expected checksums; b0file hit the 7200 s per-stage timeout while still progressing -- it did not fail, it did not finish. Metrics remain null: simulator wall time measures the simulator, not the target, and target-side cycles for user programs are deferred by the metrics contract.
applications.policy_violation: the disk was not a fresh copy: this run reused one an earlier attempt had written to, so 'disk at start' differs from the pristine B0 image. Recorded, not hidden.

limits: Both board runs share one boot session; nothing is reproduced across cold boots.
All IPS figures are derived (configured_hz / CPI), never measured wall throughput.
The 40 MHz frequency is configured, not measured by anything here.
Microbenchmarks are synthetic loops. No figure here is xv6's average CPI (ERRATA E3).
Application workloads are built but unexecuted; their metrics are null, not zero.
errata: benchmarks/ERRATA.md supersedes five conclusions stated before B0 existed
findings_added_after_first_draft: perf05_size: within a single 64-bit beat, access SIZE does not affect cost. A 1-byte load costs 19.32 cycles and an 8-byte load 19.36 -- 0.2% apart. Stores: 17.49 vs 17.56, 0.4% apart.
Stores are about 10% cheaper than loads (17.5 vs 19.4 cycles), consistent with a write being acknowledged before a read could return data.
Sub-word writes carry NO read-modify-write penalty: sb costs the same as sd, so byte strobes are being used rather than a read-modify-write below.

The expected application checksums were computed on the host with C's %lx (lowercase) while xv6's printf uses "0123456789ABCDEF". A run that produced exactly the right value failed its check on case alone. Fixed with an inline (?i) and a regression; found by running it.
